clue.text: Fed by father, old swimmer wearing rubber

indicators.note: by means next to, so the agent comes alongside the other pieces

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
a Fed is an American federal agent, a G-man

explanation.surface: A swimmer in a rubber suit is being fed by his father, an old man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed' looks like a verb but is a noun: an FBI agent, or G-MAN, placed by FR and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A frogman is a diver in a rubber wetsuit, so the definition describes the person by his gear.

clue.text: See 23
See 18
Internal memo?

parts.note: an office memo circulated internally, read instead as a note kept inside the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Internal memo' suggests office paperwork; the question mark tells you the memo is inside someone's mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminder you fix in your memory without writing it down is a note kept wholly in the mind.

clue.text: Nick's short comment on chapter

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first part sits above the chapter
short means the comment is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a note is a brief comment

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick makes a brief remark about a chapter of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' reads as a man's name, but it is a cut or groove. NOTE loses its last letter to give NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut, which is exactly what a nick is.

clue.text: Small party on the left with grouch penning article? There's 23 according to complainants!

indicators.note: on the left places the party before the small piece, the reverse of the clue's order

parts.note: a do is a party
mini means small

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the grouch holds the article inside it

parts.note: a crab is a grumpy person, a grouch
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A little left-wing party with a grumpy member, then a jibe at a politician accused of bullying.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is BULLY: Dominic Raab, a British Conservative minister, resigned in 2023 after complaints that he bullied civil servants.
explanation.definitionFit: The politician was the subject of formal bullying complaints from staff, so to those complainants he was a bully.

clue.text: Detectives meeting hood break down bit by bit

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
a mantle is a cloak or hood-like covering

explanation.surface: Police officers confront a hooded criminal who falls apart under questioning.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle something is to take it apart piece by piece.

clue.text: Offend certain characters in room if forthright

indicators.note: certain characters in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Speaking bluntly in a room may upset some of the people there.
explanation.definitionFit: To miff is to annoy or slightly upset someone, a colloquial synonym for offend.

clue.text: Invaders in North or South Yemen deposing leader

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for North
S is the compass abbreviation for South

indicators.note: deposing the leader removes the first letter of the country's name

parts.note: the country, taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: Armies invading either northern or southern Yemen and overthrowing its ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vikings who raided Britain and Ireland were Norsemen, famous as seaborne invaders.

clue.text: Rent at high level?

parts.note: rent as a split or tear, found high up on a glacier or mountain, not a payment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent at high level' suggests an expensive tenancy; here rent is a tear, and the high level is a glacier.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep open crack in a glacier is a tear in the ice found high in the mountains.

clue.text: Horse must pass round wide tree

indicators.note: passing round something means going around it, so the horse encloses the wide

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a coat of mixed colours
W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A horse has to go round a broad tree in its path.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a small tree known for red berries.

clue.text: Anglican chore? Special team needed

parts.note: a task for the CE, the Church of England, is a chore for Anglicans

explanation.surface: A tiresome job in the Church of England calls for a dedicated group.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as three words: a TASK FOR CE, CE being the Church of England, the Anglican church.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a unit formed for a particular operation, a specially assembled group.

clue.text: Coming in over time, I reach a second Irish assembly

indicators.note: coming in means the time slips inside the rest of the letters

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone arriving late says they will reach a second Irish parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over time' reads as running late, but over is O and time is T, which goes in after I REACH.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oireachtas is the national parliament of Ireland, comprising the President and two houses.

clue.text: What's writ large for Alcyone deceived Olympian queen

parts.note: Alcyone is a woman of Greek myth, so the pronoun for her is her
the capital A, written large at the head of the name Alcyone

explanation.surface: A myth note: what is magnified for Alcyone, and a queen of Olympus tricked.
explanation.walkthrough: Alcyone, a figure of Greek myth, supplies both pieces: the pronoun her and her capital initial. Zeus tricked Hera into marriage, hence deceived.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera, wife of Zeus, is queen of the gods on Mount Olympus, and Zeus seduced her by trickery.

clue.text: Patron having been upset by agent

indicators.note: by means next to, so the agent comes alongside
upset means the letters of been are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: a factor is an agent who buys and sells for another

explanation.surface: A sponsor is upset by the actions of his agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor gives money or help to a cause, which is what a patron does.

clue.text: Still he follows group on leaving class

indicators.note: follows means he comes after the group

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians

indicators.note: leaving means the word on goes out of the class

parts.note: a lesson is a class at school

explanation.surface: A man still joins a band once his lesson is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' sits as an adverb at the start, easy to read as calm or motionless; here it means however.
explanation.definitionFit: Still, in the sense of 'even so' or 'however', is synonymous with nonetheless.

clue.text: Change menu and put in scarce chemical

indicators.note: change tells you to rearrange these letters into something else

explanation.surface: A cook alters the menu and adds a rare chemical ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptunium is a radioactive element found only in trace amounts in nature.

clue.text: Hotel, poorly ventilated, unlocked perhaps?

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
airless means stuffy, lacking fresh air

explanation.surface: A stuffy hotel room, perhaps with an unlocked door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlocked' suggests a door; here it means without locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bald has no locks of hair, so 'unlocked' is a punning way of describing baldness.

clue.text: Paid with radicchio, initially, that is found among mixed greens

indicators.note: found among means the inner letters sit inside the salad

parts.note: a salad is a mix of green leaves

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of radicchio

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A recipe: radicchio added to mixed salad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaried worker receives a fixed regular wage, so they are paid.

clue.text: Cope with wife distressed in city after Satan deviously displays what he is?

indicators.note: after means the rest of the wordplay comes following Satan
deviously suggests Satan's letters are twisted into a crooked order
in means the reworked letters go inside the city

parts.note: York is a cathedral city in northern England

indicators.note: distressed means cope and wife are agitated into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Surviving with an upset wife in a city, after Satan reveals his true nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cope' looks like a verb meaning manage, but it is just letters to rearrange with 'wife'; the result sits inside the city after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling the Devil an unpleasant, malicious person is a fair understatement of his character.

clue.text: Hot duck St Leonard eats?

indicators.note: eats means the saint's name takes the duck inside

parts.note: St, as written, the abbreviation for saint
Len is a short form of Leonard
in cricket a duck is a score of zero, written O

explanation.surface: Does St Leonard eat a hot duck dinner?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot duck' reads as a dish; hot is slang for stolen, and duck is a cricket zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot goods are recently stolen ones, a slang sense used of goods traceable by police.

clue.text: Pressure needed in bellows? I'm astounded!

indicators.note: needed in means the pressure has to go inside the bellows

parts.note: bellows as a verb means shouts or cries
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Bellows need pressure to work, a fact that astonishes someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bellows' looks like the fireside tool, but it is a verb: shouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cripes is a dated exclamation of surprise, roughly 'goodness me'.

clue.text: See 5
Thick liquid drowning upright character in hotel lift

parts.note: thick means stupid, dumb

indicators.note: drowning means the water surrounds the upright character

parts.note: water is the commonest liquid
the letter I is an upright stroke

explanation.surface: Someone stupid is drowned in a thick liquid in a hotel lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbwaiter is a small lift carrying food between floors in a hotel or restaurant.

clue.text: Farm animal behind another heard outside yard? Well done!

indicators.note: outside means the animal words stand around the yard, which slips in between them

parts.note: a bull is a farm animal
behind, as in supporting, means for

indicators.note: heard means the word for another farm animal is taken by its sound

parts.note: another farm animal, a ewe

explanation.surface: One farm animal stands behind another, overheard outside the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' means in support of, giving FOR; the other farm animal is a female sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Bully for you is an exclamation of congratulation, often used sarcastically.

clue.text: Colorado state prosecutor closing bars

parts.note: CO is the US postal abbreviation for Colorado
a DA is a district attorney, an American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A Colorado prosecutor shuts down drinking bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closing bars' suggests shutting pubs; the bars are musical measures.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a piece of music.

clue.text: Leader in media having no case to retreat back

indicators.note: having no case means the outer letters of media are stripped away
back means the retreat is read in reverse

parts.note: a lair is a hideaway, a retreat

explanation.surface: A media leader, without a defence, has to retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader is a newspaper's leading article, giving the paper's own opinion.

clue.text: Bulb producing this lit up explosively

indicators.note: explosively means the letters are blown apart and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A light bulb lit up and exploded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' suggests a light bulb; the bulb is one you plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tulip grows from a bulb planted in autumn.

clue.text: Weapon not deployed at the front?

definitions.text: Weapon not deployed at the front?

parts.words: Weapon not deployed at the front?
parts.note: a gun not sent to the front line, read as one worn not at the front of the body but on the hip

explanation.walkthrough: 'at the front' suggests the battlefield front line; the weapon is worn at the side of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol worn in a holster on the hip is carried at the belt, beside the body.

clue.text: We might say this about yellow pants

parts.words: We might say this about yellow
parts.note: the word yellow has a Y at its front, so one could describe it in those two words

explanation.surface: A comment on someone's yellow underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English pants are underpants; Y-fronts are men's briefs with an inverted-Y seam.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are a style of men's briefs, so they are a kind of underwear.
